entries.title: DRAFT: Boundary wiring density and its q=1 degeneracy
entries.statement: DRAFT, independent mathematical review pending. On a finite FK graph with fixed edge probabilities, q>0 and boundary partition xi, merging u,v gives R=Z_eta/Z_xi=1/q+(1-1/q)*P_xi(u connected to v). For a common predictable edge-revelation filtration, the density is D_n=[1/q+(1-1/q)*P_xi(u connected to v|F_n)]/R. At q=1 it is identically one, so this density alone supplies no Loewner variance constraint.
assumptions: Count every connected component, including identified boundary components
Same edge factors and same predictable revelation rule

entries.title: DRAFT: Two profiles identify a localized Loewner driver
entries.statement: DRAFT, independent mathematical review pending. Let continuous adapted W_0=0 drive dg_t(z)=2/(g_t(z)-W_t)dt. For 0<x1<x2<y, set X_i=g_t(x_i)-W_t,Y=g_t(y)-W_t,U_i=X_i/Y. Stop before swallowing and localize with positive X_i,Y and U_i in compact subsets of (0,1). For kappa>0 let H prime be u^(-4/kappa)(1-u)^(8/kappa-2). If both H(U_i) are continuous local martingales in the same filtration, the independent calculation recovers W as a semimartingale and gives zero drift and bracket kappa dt on that stopped interval. This supplies no FK profile convergence theorem.
assumptions: Common filtration and compact unswallowed localization
Conclusion only on the stopped interval

entries.title: DRAFT: One profile does not identify the driver
entries.statement: DRAFT, independent mathematical review pending. For 0<x<y and t<xy/4, the smooth deterministic driver W_t=(x+y)(1-sqrt(1-4t/(xy))) has Loewner images with X_t=x*sqrt(1-4t/(xy)) and Y_t=y*sqrt(1-4t/(xy)). Therefore U_t=x/y is constant and every finite H(U_t) is a local martingale, while W has nonzero finite variation and bracket zero. The second independent observable in the two-profile criterion cannot simply be dropped.
assumptions: Counterexample targets a one-profile inference, not the actual two-profile criterion

relations.rationale: The one-profile card says "the second independent observable ... cannot simply be dropped"; the two-profile card explicitly requires "two distinct ordered marked points". The counterexample does not refute the stated two-profile criterion.
The gap card requires "two actual FK observables" converging to the "specified conformal profiles"; the conditional driver criterion begins "If both H(U_i) are continuous local martingales".
The gap card distinguishes finite martingales from identified profiles; the wiring card states that q=1 density is "identically one".
Existing C0049 node names Dobrushin exploration convergence; this audit records that the October 6 theorem is a free-boundary loop theorem. No relation asserts a full solution.
